title: Rav Chisda ben Avira
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is cited in [Yalkut Shmuel, remez 118](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.118.2), as saying: “Tasting does not count as eating,” etc.[^1] Hyman traces the saying to [Yerushalmi Nedarim 8:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.8.1.6), where it reads Rabbi Ba Chasida in the name of Rabbi Zeira. Without doubt, he argues, a conflation involving Zeira produced Avira, and Rabbi Ba Chasida became Rav Chisda. Midrash Shmuel likewise gives “Rabbi Ba Chasida bar Rabbi Zeira.” Hyman explains ב״ר here as an abbreviation for בשם ר׳, “in the name of R'.”[^2]

notes.text: The printed Yalkut number is 108; the corresponding passage is remez 118 in the digital text. Hyman cites the beginning of Nedarim, chapter 1; the matching passage is [8:1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.8.1.6).
Hyman reads ב״ר here as בשם ר׳, “in the name of,” rather than as a patronymic. Midrash Shmuel has “Ba Chasida bar Rabbi Zeira”; the Yerushalmi has “Rabbi Ba Chasida in the name of Rabbi Zeira.”
